_source: groundSpring Experiment 038 — LTEE Clonal Interference (Good et al. 2017)
_references: Good BH, McDonald MJ, Barrick JE, Lenski RE, Desai MM (2017) The dynamics of molecular evolution over 60,000 generations. Nature 551:45-50
Desai MM, Fisher DS (2007) Beneficial Mutation-Selection Balance and the Effect of Linkage on Positive Selection. Genetics 176:1759-1798
Gerrish PJ, Lenski RE (1998) The fate of competing beneficial mutations in an asexual population. Genetica 102/103:127-144

_provenance.generated_by: Synthetic clonal interference simulation using Wright-Fisher model with multiple concurrent beneficial mutations
_provenance.data_origin: Synthetic data reproducing the clonal interference regime described by Good et al. 2017 and Desai & Fisher 2007 theory
_provenance.real_data_accession: N/A (synthetic from published parameter regime; real LTEE metagenomic data at SRA PRJNA380528 for future Tier 2)

_description: Reproduce the clonal interference analysis from Good et al. (2017): in large asexual populations, multiple beneficial mutations arise simultaneously and compete for fixation. The key result is that the fixation probability of a beneficial mutation decreases relative to the neutral expectation (1/N) as population size increases, because of competition from other contemporaneous beneficials. We simulate Wright-Fisher populations at multiple sizes with a constant supply of beneficial mutations and measure effective fixation probability vs the Desai-Fisher theoretical prediction.
_groundspring_question: How does clonal interference affect the dynamics of adaptation in large asexual populations? What is the effective fixation probability of a beneficial mutation when competing clones are present?
_cross_spring: lithoSpore module 3 (clonal-dynamics), hotSpring B2 (fitness landscape), groundSpring B1 (neutral fixation baseline)

model._description: Simulate Wright-Fisher populations at 4 population sizes. Each generation: mutations arise at rate U_b per genome per generation. Beneficial mutations have selective advantage s drawn from exponential distribution. Track lineages to fixation. Compare observed fixation probability to neutral (1/N) and Desai-Fisher clonal interference prediction.
model._theory_note: In the clonal interference regime (N * U_b >> 1), the Desai-Fisher (2007) prediction is that the rate of adaptation v ~ s * (2 * ln(N*s) * s / ln(s / U_b))^(1/2), and the effective fixation probability of a single beneficial mutation is much less than 2*s (the Haldane sieve for non-interfering mutations).

expected_results._adaptation_note: Compare within interference regime (N*U_b >= 1). N=100 is mutation-limited; ratio across regimes is not meaningful for sublinearity test.
